# A midpoint-only reflection bound fails; the exact reflection maximum survives

The actual convex body with integer interval fibers of lengths `(2,6,10,3)`
refutes the proposed scalar midpoint bound. Its full central-reflection
maximum, allowing the center to move within an integer fiber, is instead
`12/21=4/7` of total mass. Thus this example does **not** refute half-mass
central-reflection retention for arbitrary interval-fiber bodies.

## 1. Body and the failed scalar shortcut

Let

    C=conv{(0,0),(3,0),(3,3),(2,10),(0,2)}.

Its positive integer fibers are exactly

    I_0=[0,2], I_1=[0,6], I_2=[0,10], I_3=[0,3].

The upper boundary has slopes 4,4,-7, so these lengths form a concave
sequence. The total mixed length is `M=21`.

For a general compatible interval family with lengths w_z, reflecting
about the midpoint of I_j gives the lower bound

    B_j=w_j+2 sum_(k>=1) min(w_(j-k),w_(j+k),
                             (w_(j-k)+w_(j+k)-w_j)_+),       (1)

where missing positive fibers give zero terms. Indeed, compatibility
places `(I_(j-k)+I_(j+k))/2` inside I_j, and the two-interval overlap
formula in `candidate ad15334eed60c161`
applies to each pair independently.

For the present body, (1) gives

    (B_0,B_1,B_2,B_3)=(2,10,10,3).

These are also the actual reflection masses at the four fiber midpoints.
Consequently `max_j B_j=10<21/2`. Concavity of the length sequence does
not imply the proposed scalar inequality `max_j B_j>=M/2`.

## 2. Exact unrestricted reflection calculation

Write

    R_j(y)=sum_z |I_z intersect (2y-I_(2j-z))|,

for `(j,y)` in the actual mixed source. Missing fibers contribute zero.
For two intervals `[0,a]`, `[0,c]`, the summand equals

    [min(a,c,2y,a+c-2y)]_+.                           (2)

The paired summands at z and 2j-z are equal. At an extreme base only the
self-reflection contributes, hence

    max R_0=2 at y=1,       max R_3=3 at y=3/2.

At base 1 the self interval has length 6 and the other pair has lengths
2 and 10. Formula (2) gives the complete piecewise expression

    R_1(y)=6y,             0<=y<=1;
           2y+4,           1<=y<=3;
           16-2y,          3<=y<=5;
           36-6y,          5<=y<=6.                  (3)

Its unique maximum is `R_1(3)=10`.

At base 2 the self interval has length 10 and the other pair has lengths
6 and 3. The complete expression is

    R_2(y)=6y,             0<=y<=3/2;
           2y+6,           3/2<=y<=3;
           18-2y,          3<=y<=9/2;
           2y,             9/2<=y<=5;
           20-2y,          5<=y<=10.                 (4)

Its unique global maximum is `R_2(3)=12`. At this center the self overlap
is `[0,6]`, of length 6, and the two paired overlaps each have length 3.
The midpoint `y=5` is a smaller local maximum of mass 10.

Together (3)--(4) and the extreme-base calculations prove

    max_((j,y) in C intersect Lambda) R_j(y)=12,
    R_max/M=4/7>1/2.                                 (5)

In particular the retained symmetric source at `(2,3)` alone certifies
ordinary mixed halfspace depth at least `6/21=2/7` at that point. No claim
that this is its exact depth is needed here. The result closes the
midpoint-only scalar shortcut, while leaving the general reflection
retention question undecided.

The exact Fraction verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_four_fiber_reflection_bound_failure.py`.
